question: About how many people can a group hold together through gossip and personal ties alone?
answer: About 150, the figure researchers associate with Robin Dunbar. Below it, people can know each other and keep order through reputation. Above it, Harari argues, groups need shared myths, a god, a flag, a company brand, to make strangers cooperate. Armies, firms and cities rest on that trick.
move: Past about 150 people, rules and stories must replace knowing each other.
trap: 'About 1,500': a village feels knowable, but it isn't.
simply: You can keep track of who's kind and who cheats in your class. In a whole city you can't, so people use laws and shared stories instead.
why: It is why small teams can run on trust while big organisations need rules and a story. Knowing the limit helps you see when a group has outgrown its habits.
reference: Yuval Noah Harari, Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind (Harper, 2015), ch. 2
